title: Solar Rebates in Toronto 2026: Up to $10,000, With No Net Metering
desc: Toronto solar and battery rebates for 2026 under Home Renovation Savings: $1,000 per kW up to $5,000, battery $300 per kWh up to $5,000, and the rule that excludes net metering.
lead: Toronto gets about 3.91 peak sun hours a day, one of the better figures in our Ontario data. The rebate is worth up to $10,000, but only for a system designed to offset the home's own use.
cards_heading: What Home Renovation Savings pays for solar and batteries in Toronto
cards_intro: We re-read the program's solar page and its October 2025 requirements on October 3, 2026. The rebate comes with conditions that change how the system is designed, so read them before you ask for quotes.

cards.title: Solar panels
cards.note: Paid on installed DC capacity, capped at 50% of eligible costs. Rooftop systems only, including a garage roof on the same meter.

cards.title: Battery storage
cards.note: Only with a new solar system, also capped at 50% of eligible costs. Combined solar and battery rebates reach $10,000.

cards.title: No net metering
cards.amount: Rebate excluded if you net meter
cards.note: A system under an Ontario net metering agreement is not eligible. The system must be sized for load displacement only.

cards.title: Approvals before you buy
cards.note: The contractor files the pre-installation application with a quote dated within 60 days. You cannot buy or install before IESO pre-approval and your local utility's approval.

cards.title: Finish within 12 months
cards.note: The project must be complete within 12 months of approval, with the ESA certificate and the connection agreement filed within 30 days of installation.

cards.title: First-time installs only
cards.note: Homes that already have solar or storage are not eligible. Leases, rentals and lease-to-own arrangements are excluded.

cards.title: Toronto HELP loan
cards.note: A City loan for energy upgrades. Current rates were not re-verified.

after_cards: The requirements document gives no end date for this stream, and funding conditions can change, so confirm on the program page before you sign. The IESO has no pre-qualified contractor list for it.
sections: Roofs in a city of apartments

Only about 35% of Toronto's 1,160,895 households live in a house type the program accepts, and 47% live in tall apartments. The Census counts 270,355 detached households. For those, roof orientation, shading from neighbouring buildings and the age of the roof decide the system size. With 58% of households in homes built before 1981, check the roof's remaining life first.

The contractor must submit a connection application to your local distribution company, which in Toronto is Toronto Hydro, and the project needs its approval before you buy. Ask Toronto Hydro about the connection process and the largest system it will allow on your service, as the program suggests.

Toronto's Home Energy Loan Program lets owners repay upgrades through the property tax bill, which can carry the cost until the rebate is paid after the post-installation approval. We have not re-verified the current rate, so check the City's page. Loan interest is not an eligible cost for the rebate.

Many Ontario solar quotes assume net metering, where extra power sent to the grid earns bill credits. This program does not allow it: a system under a net metering agreement is not eligible, and the system must be sized for load displacement, meaning it should match what the home uses. A Toronto owner who wants the rebate should tell every installer up front, because a system designed to export will not qualify.

The panels must be on the roof of the house or of a permanent structure on the same property and connected to the home's meter, such as a detached garage. Ground mounts are not eligible, and neither are systems on trailers or other temporary structures. Toronto has 270,355 detached houses, where roof orientation and shading decide the system size.

The rebate is capped at 50% of eligible costs, which cover equipment, permits, approvals and labour. HST, financing costs, insurance, maintenance and spare parts are not eligible costs. A quote should therefore show the pre-HST price and separate any financing, so the program can check that $1,000 per kW does not exceed half.

The order matters. The contractor submits the pre-installation application with a quote dated within 60 days, you receive written pre-approval and your utility's approval, and only then do you buy and install. The system must be finished within 12 months of approval, and the contractor files the post-installation application within 30 days of installation.
claim_steps: Confirm you own an eligible house type with a roof or garage that suits panels.
Talk to Toronto Hydro about the connection process and the maximum system size allowed before you sign anything.
Choose a licensed electrical contractor and ask for a quote that shows the DC capacity in kW and the eligible costs without HST.
Let the contractor file the pre-installation application, and wait for written IESO pre-approval and utility approval before buying or installing.
After the install, check that the post-installation application is filed within 30 days with the ESA certificate and connection agreement.
faq: Can I net meter and still get the rebate?
No. A system under a net metering agreement is not eligible.
Can I put panels on a garage?
Yes, if it is a permanent structure on the same meter.
$10,000 combined, $5,000 each for solar and battery.
